title: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly: your original beside the candidate
intro: Your original is on the left and the candidate is on the right. Struck words are yours that were cut; highlighted words are new, from Emulate or from my fixes.
Under each changed paragraph is what I'd do and why. Anything I don't mention, I'd keep. Nothing here is applied yet, and every fix gets a Pangram recheck, alone and in the section.
One correction: I was wrong about the East Wind deletion you approved. See the power paragraph.

headings: ## The New Age May Dawn Suddenly

rows.label: P1 · opening
rows.article: I just put a movie my father made in 1988
notes: Keep, with one fix to my own slip: put back your “the same” (“recreating the same loneliness, domination, and stupidity”). I wrote “all the”; your “the same” is the point, that they could rebuild what they were fleeing.
You approved “for him was primary”. I'd keep “all kinds of communes” and “around the country”: they don't change what happened.

rows.label: P4 · escuelita
rows.article: This is the escuelita referenced in my title.
source: That’s where the escuelita in my title comes in.
notes: Rebuild it from yours. Emulate changed four things that matter.
“This is the escuelita” points at nothing. Yours says where the escuelita comes in.
“I’m borrowing the word” is gone.
Learning autonomy “by living it” became learning “how the Zapatistas practice” it.
“The healing communities I’m proposing” became “these healing communities”, so it no longer says they're your proposal. And the “relational and practical methods” became “the methods they’re using”.

How I'd do it: start from Emulate's version, put your sentences back one at a time and recheck each on Pangram. Whatever can't go back as your sentence goes back as a small fix inside Emulate's. Your closing line is already back.

rows.label: P5 · childhood
source: That’s how I spent much of my childhood
notes: “Every community we could” is a new claim about your family. I'd say “and many others”, as you did.
Put back “usually” (“usually just a visitor’s kid”): your family lived at Love Israel for two years, two paragraphs down.
Put back “never quite part of the tribe”. It's your phrase, and more exact than “not part of any tribe”.
Keep the rest, including your approved “grew up on shoulders” and “boring as hell”.

rows.label: P10 · East Wind
rows.article: The East Wind commune was almost the opposite way.
source: East Wind felt almost like the opposite social experience.
notes: “Happy” for “very happy”: it's your report of how you felt.
“Real variety” for “diverse”, which can read as ethnicity.
Drop “big”, which Emulate added to the shower.
Keep the rest, including your approved history-books line.

rows.label: P11 · East Wind's power problem
rows.article: Even at East Wind, though, there was a power issue.
source: East Wind still had a quieter power problem.
notes: Put the reason back: “They had a nut butter factory that brought in a lot of their income, which seemed to make the woman running it very hard to question.” Emulate kept the income and the woman but dropped the “which seemed to make her”, and your last clause was the only other place the reason survived.
Put back “quieter” (“there was a quieter power issue”), which sets it against Love Israel's.
With the reason back, your last clause really is a repeat, so I'd leave it out. Ending on “no obvious guru” reads well.

rows.label: P12 · Acorn
rows.article: There were like eight people at the Acorn commune
source: Acorn had something like eight people
notes: “Own” for “live on”: it's a fact about them.

Keep the rest. Emulate has you lean (“I didn't feel like it was really a commune I could join”) where you said you couldn't tell, and adds “It would have been hard to join”, but your group-chat line already leans the same way.

rows.label: P13 · Twin Oaks
notes: “Friendly and interesting” without the two “enough”s, which make you sound lukewarm.
“At the time” after the head count, since it's a number from then.
Keep the rest.

rows.label: P14 · the missing practice
rows.article: One thing that struck me as odd
source: Across nearly all of these places
notes: In “came into the commune with them”, “them” reads as the communities. I'd write: “People brought all the usual human pain and suffering in with them, and it all got translated into politics.”
Keep “all of them, basically”: “basically” keeps your “nearly”.

rows.label: P15 · the meetings
notes: Put back your remembered thought in your words: “…and the persistent thought, “I’d rather be sleeping.””
“Needed” for “wanted”: “most of what anyone actually needed to talk about couldn't be talked about”.
Keep “Which meant”: it ties the meetings to the politics before it.
